findings.F1: Over all bars, not only after 5-day falls, the 5-day/30-day log volume ratio predicts the coin's excess 3-day return upward: the pooled slope is 0.0124 (t 4.32, n 4283 non-overlapping cases); it is 0.0170 after falls (t 4.07, n 2071) and 0.0072 after rises (t 1.80, n 2212), while the ratio multiplied by the sign of the 5-day return gives t -1.99, so the effect follows volume, not the fall the idea names.
findings.F2: The volume-ratio effect holds at 7 days too (slope 0.0233, t 3.22, n 1723), but it is concentrated in a few places: XRP (t 3.75) and ZEC (t 2.36), against t 0.36 to 1.32 for BTC, ETH, LTC and XMR, and windows w19-24 (t 4.39) against t 1.00 to 1.92 in the other three window groups.
findings.F3: The 5-day return predicts the excess 3-day return in the same direction (slope 0.0236, t 2.30, n 5435; top quintile +0.00734, t 2.46), and this momentum sits entirely on thin-volume bars: slope 0.0550 (t 2.80, n 2513) when the volume ratio is ≤ 0, against 0.0019 (t 0.13, n 1770) when it is above 0.
findings.F4: Against the brief, a compressed range is not followed by larger moves: the mean absolute 3-day return is 0.0538 in the most compressed 5/30-day range quintile and 0.0663 in the most expanded, the excess absolute return rises with the range ratio (t 5.61) and with the volume ratio (t 6.89), and the next 3 days' range follows the past range ratio (t 20.96).
findings.F5: The book's mean daily return of 0.00017 sits far below the coins' own mean daily returns of 0.00067 to 0.00155, because it is short on 28-36 % of bars against long on 18-21 % (mean position -0.035 to -0.086); its gain from the market's own rise is -0.000076 a day.

ideas.idea: The higher a coin's 5-day average volume against its 30-day average, the higher its return over the next 3 days, whatever the direction of its last 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean long a coin whose recent volume is heavy against its month and away from a coin trading on thin volume, instead of reading thin volume only as a warning on dips.
ideas.name: Heavy volume precedes gains

ideas.idea: While a coin's 5-day average volume is below its 30-day average, the larger its 5-day return, the larger its return over the next 3 days in the same direction.
ideas.consequence: A trader would follow quiet, low-volume drifts in their own direction rather than fade them.
ideas.name: Quiet-volume momentum continues

ideas.idea: The wider a coin's 5-day average daily range against its 30-day average, the larger its absolute price move over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would size positions down and widen stops after a range expansion, not after a compression.
ideas.name: Range expansion keeps expanding
